analytical_conclusions.duration_and_energy: Direct measurement: Duration, RMS energy, attack time, and onset spectral centroid are statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE between TRAI and PHAI. Generator parameters confirm identical envelopes and noise seeds.
analytical_conclusions.formant_trajectories: Code inspection and spectrogram analysis: Both TRAI and PHAI use identical F1=800Hz, F2=1350Hz, F3=2600Hz with identical glide towards /j/.
analytical_conclusions.consonant_onset: Phonetic limitation: Natural Vietnamese contrasts /tɕ/ (voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate stop) with /f/ (voiceless labiodental fricative). The generator synthesizes both with the exact same 50ms decaying Gaussian noise burst (Northern/Central). Zero spectral frication or stop closure exists.
analytical_conclusions.pitch_f0_contour: Direct measurement: Pitch contour is the ONLY acoustic discriminator in the synthetic generator. TRAI rises monotonically (+35%). PHAI dips at mid-utterance (-20%) before rising (+15%).
analytical_conclusions.generalization_defect_root_cause: Because the model has zero consonant spectral cues, it must rely entirely on F0 trajectory. When training on 14 fixed speakers without pitch augmentation, TC-ResNet-14 memorized the specific mel bands where harmonics moved. In unseen speakers with base F0 between 140Hz and 195Hz, the dipping harmonic curve falls into novel mel channels. TC-ResNet's global temporal average/max pooling collapses time order, so it fails to recognize the dip.
